narrative:
After reviewing your application, the model determined there is a 58% chance you would be a bad credit risk. This means that, statistically, you are more likely than not to have difficulty repaying the loan, so your application was denied.

The most important reason was the status of your checking account. You currently have a negative balance, a situation seen in only about 13% of approved applicants. This strongly pushed the decision toward denial, as it suggests immediate financial strain. The second biggest factor was the duration of the loan you requested. You asked for 42 months, while approved applicants typically request around 19 months. This longer commitment made the model see more uncertainty in your ability to repay over time.

Interestingly, your credit history actually worked in your favor. Although it is rated as critical, this pattern is relatively common among approved borrowers, so the model treated it as a mitigating factor rather than a reason to deny. However, this positive influence was not strong enough to overcome the two major risk signals.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on building a positive checking account balance and waiting until your financial situation is more stable. Consider applying for a smaller loan with a shorter repayment period, perhaps 12 to 18 months, and ensure your account shows a surplus for several months before reapplying. These changes would directly address the two most important reasons for today’s decision.
